purpose: Empirically arbitrate code-scanner CODE-006 vs econ-scanner ECON-001/ECON-002 by encoding realizable-rate invariants in a harness where the AMM execution rate is set INDEPENDENTLY of the vault convertToAssets/Shares rate.

harness.design: MockERC4626Vault defines the VAULT rate p (kept at 1:1, never simulateYield); MockAMMAdapter defines the AMM REALIZABLE rate q with an independently-settable sell rate. r := q/p. Strategy holds restricted shares realizable only at q.

invariants.name: invariant_realizableSolvency
invariants.description: INV-1: liquidating ALL remaining shares at the current AMM rate (held*q) must cover all remaining credited principal (totalDeposited). The strategy only asserts this at the VAULT rate (held*p), not the realizable AMM rate.

invariants.name: no_cross_client_principal_drain
invariants.description: INV-2: a single client's favorable-rate (r>1) withdraw must not reduce the realizable backing of OTHER clients' principal.

invariants.name: surplus_routing
invariants.description: INV-3: value above aggregate principal (skimmable surplus) must only ever leave via skimSurplus, never via an ordinary withdraw.

results_detail.MarketRateArbitrage.test_ECON001_skim_br: PASS (demonstrates INV-1 flips from solvent to broken across a skim; logged shortfall 28.5e18)
results_detail.MarketRateArbitrage.test_ECON001_skim_tu: PASS (demonstrates last-out proportional exit drops 970e18 -> 921.5e18 because skim stripped the buffer; logged delta 48.5e18)

results_detail.MarketRateArbitrage.test_ECON002_ordinar: PASS (INV-3 broken: ordinary withdraw pocketed 100e18 of skimmable surplus outside skim)

depositForClient(...)   -> principal credited 626988.6e18, held 626988.6e18 after skim

ECON-001.claim: skimSurplus prices the deposit haircut buffer at the vault rate and skims it out as yield; afterwards, under an AMM discount, the last-out staker realizes less than principal -> socialized shortfall.
ECON-001.evidence: Both forge and medusa independently break realizable-solvency with the minimal sequence deposit -> skim -> AMM-discount. The skim removes exactly the over-collateralization buffer (held*p - D) that was absorbing the discount: pre-skim held*q=970e18 >= D=950e18 (solvent), post-skim held*q=921.5e18 < D=950e18 (insolvent). Concretely, the proportional last-out exit (totalWithdrawal) realizes 970e18 WITHOUT a prior skim vs only 921.5e18 WITH a prior skim for the same 3% discount -> a 48.5e18 swing, of which the staker eats a 28.5e18 shortfall while the skim recipient walked with the buffer.
ECON-001.mechanism_note: Root cause is the profile's scannerAttention #1: minOut, surplus, totalBalanceOf and the 'solvency invariant' are all denominated at the VAULT rate (convertToAssets) while funds realize only at the AMM rate. skimSurplus's aggregate-surplus ceiling (convertToShares(totalValue-td)) is a VAULT-rate ceiling, so a 'surplus' that does not exist at realizable rates is harvested, digging into realizable principal-backing.
ECON-001.severity: Medium (value leak / staker principal shortfall, with an external precondition: sUSDe trading below NAV, realistic given the 7-day cooldown)

ECON-002.claim: a withdrawer pockets amount*(r-1) when sUSDe trades above vault fair value, defeating skimSurplus as the surplus-routing path.
ECON-002.evidence: At r=1.1 an ordinary withdraw of 1000e18 principal pays the withdrawer 1100e18 while debiting only 1000e18; the protocol's skimmable surplus dropped by exactly the pocketed 100e18 (surplus left OUTSIDE skimSurplus). INV-3 broken.
ECON-002.severity_note: The extra value is paid by the AMM counterparty (see CODE-006), not taken from another client's share backing, and all authorized clients are protocol-owned, so the leak is a misallocation of protocol surplus (to the withdrawing client's stakers instead of the skim recipient) rather than external theft. Real surplus-routing defeat, but severity tempered to Medium/Low depending on whether the skim recipient is the same beneficiary as the client's stakers.

CODE-006.claim: REFUTED: vault-rate surplus S*p - D is invariant under any withdrawal at any AMM price q; the withdraw upside is the AMM counterparty overpaying on the withdrawer's OWN share sale, not other-client value.
CODE-006.verdict: CORRECT ON ITS NARROW TERMS, but it is the wrong frame for the risk
CODE-006.evidence: INV-2 HOLDS: after A withdraws its full principal at r=1.1, client B's principal backing is untouched and B still realizes >= its principal. The vault-rate surplus S*p - D is indeed invariant under a withdraw (verified algebraically and empirically). So CODE-006 correctly refutes a cross-client-principal-theft reading of ECON-002.
CODE-006.but: CODE-006 measures solvency at the VAULT rate, which is exactly the quantity that overstates realizable backing. The actual risks (ECON-001 last-out solvency, ECON-002 surplus mis-routing) live at the AMM-realizable rate and at the surplus-routing invariant, neither of which CODE-006's vault-rate identity addresses. The 'conflict' dissolves: CODE-006 refutes a claim ECON-002 does not need; ECON-002's real claim (surplus leaks outside skim) and ECON-001 (skim strips the discount buffer) both stand.
